statements.label: supported
statements.text: The study examined 177 members of the Berne Amish community, of whom 43 carried the null SERPINE1 mutation.
statements.evidence: We studied 177 members of the Berne Amish community, which included 43 carriers of the null SERPINE1 mutation.
statements.note: The abstract states 177 members were studied, including 43 carriers of the null SERPINE1 mutation.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The null SERPINE1 mutation was also linked to a lower prevalence of cardiovascular disease in carriers.
statements.evidence: Our study indicates a causal effect of PAI-1 on human longevity, which may be mediated by alterations in metabolism.
statements.note: The abstract ties longevity to metabolic changes and never reports any cardiovascular disease outcome.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Heterozygous carriers had lower fasting insulin levels and a lower prevalence of diabetes mellitus than non-carriers.
statements.evidence: Heterozygosity was associated with significantly longer leukocyte telomere length, lower fasting insulin levels, and lower prevalence of diabetes mellitus.
statements.note: Heterozygosity was associated with lower fasting insulin and lower diabetes prevalence.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Within the extended Amish kindred, carriers of the null SERPINE1 allele lived longer.
statements.evidence: In the extended Amish kindred, carriers of the null SERPINE1 allele had a longer life span.
statements.note: The abstract reports a longer life span for null-allele carriers in the extended kindred.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: HSCs from clonal hematopoiesis samples, whether mutant or not, were enriched for inflammatory and aging signatures versus non-CH HSCs.
statements.evidence: both mutant and non-mutant HSCs from CH samples are enriched for inflammatory and aging transcriptomic signatures, compared with HSCs from non-CH samples
statements.note: The abstract reports CH-sample HSCs are enriched for inflammatory and aging signatures compared with non-CH HSCs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: TET2 mutations sped up myeloid maturation in a dose-dependent way.
statements.evidence: TET2 mutations accelerate myeloid maturation in a dose-dependent manner.
statements.note: The abstract states TET2 mutations accelerate myeloid maturation dose-dependently.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Carriers of DNMT3A or TET2 clonal hematopoiesis mutations had a higher rate of progression to acute myeloid leukemia.
statements.evidence: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) arises when hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) acquire mutations, most frequently in the DNMT3A and TET2 genes, conferring a competitive advantage through mechanisms that remain unclear.
statements.note: The abstract covers clonal expansion and selective advantage but never mentions progression to leukemia.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mutant DNMT3A and TET2 HSCs mounted a weaker inflammatory response than wild-type HSCs in the same sample.
statements.evidence: DNMT3A- and TET2-mutant HSCs have an attenuated inflammatory response relative to wild-type HSCs within the same sample.
statements.note: The abstract reports an attenuated inflammatory response in mutant HSCs relative to wild-type HSCs.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The supercentenarians' delayed aging was also seen in their first-degree relatives and offspring.
statements.evidence: A blood single-cell RNA sequencing dataset for seven supercentenarians (SCs) was recently generated.
statements.note: The study analyzes the supercentenarians themselves and never examines their relatives or offspring.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The aging clock estimated the supercentenarians' blood biological age at 80.43 to 102.67 years.
statements.evidence: Our clock model placed the SCs at a blood biological age to between 80.43 and 102.67 years.
statements.note: The abstract gives the clock-estimated biological age range of 80.43 to 102.67 years.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Relative to the expected trajectory, supercentenarians had increased naive CD8+ T cells and decreased cytotoxic CD8+ T cells.
statements.evidence: SCs display increased naive CD8 + T cells, decreased cytotoxic CD8 + T cells, memory CD4 + T cells, and megakaryocytes.
statements.note: The abstract reports increased naive and decreased cytotoxic CD8+ T cells in supercentenarians.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Supercentenarians held more cells with high ribosome levels, which was linked to low inflammation and slow aging.
statements.evidence: SCs contain more cells and cell types with high ribosome level, which is associated with and, according to Bayesian network inference, contributes to a low inflammation state and slow aging of SCs.
statements.note: The abstract states supercentenarians have more high-ribosome cells associated with low inflammation and slow aging.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Senescent cells accumulate cholesterol in lysosomes to sustain the senescence-associated secretory phenotype.
statements.evidence: senescent cells accumulate cholesterol in lysosomes to maintain the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)
statements.note: The abstract reports lysosomal cholesterol accumulation maintains the SASP.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Inducing senescence through various triggers increased cellular cholesterol metabolism.
statements.evidence: induction of cellular senescence by diverse triggers enhances cellular cholesterol metabolism
statements.note: The abstract states diverse senescence triggers enhance cholesterol metabolism.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Senescence upregulated the cholesterol exporter ABCA1, which was rerouted to the lysosome to act as a cholesterol importer.
statements.evidence: Senescence is associated with the upregulation of the cholesterol exporter ABCA1, which is rerouted to the lysosome, where it moonlights as a cholesterol importer.
statements.note: The abstract reports ABCA1 upregulation and its rerouting to the lysosome as a cholesterol importer.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Lowering dietary cholesterol intake reduced the senescent-cell burden in the mice.
statements.evidence: We further show that pharmacological modulation of lysosomal cholesterol partitioning alters senescence-associated inflammation and in vivo senescence during osteoarthritis progression in male mice.
statements.note: The study manipulates lysosomal cholesterol partitioning pharmacologically and never tests dietary cholesterol intake.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Aging lowered nerve density in the ventricle and disrupted vascular-derived neuroregulatory genes.
statements.evidence: aging reduces nerve density in the ventricle and dysregulates vascular-derived neuroregulatory genes
statements.note: The abstract reports aging reduces ventricular nerve density and dysregulates neuroregulatory genes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The age-related loss of ventricular nerve density was greater in male hearts than in female hearts.
statements.evidence: We report that aging reduces nerve density in the ventricle and dysregulates vascular-derived neuroregulatory genes.
statements.note: The abstract reports aging effects on nerve density but never compares male and female hearts.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Aging decreased miR-145 and released the neurorepulsive factor semaphorin-3A from repression.
statements.evidence: Aging down-regulates microRNA 145 (miR-145) and derepresses the neurorepulsive factor semaphorin-3A.
statements.note: The abstract states aging down-regulates miR-145 and derepresses semaphorin-3A.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Clearing senescent cells reversed age-induced denervation, preserved heart rate patterns, and lowered electrical instability.
statements.evidence: Removal of senescent cells, which accumulated with chronological age in parallel to the decline in nerve density, rescued age-induced denervation, reversed Sema3a expression, preserved heart rate patterns, and reduced electrical instability.
statements.note: The abstract reports senescent-cell removal rescued denervation, preserved heart rate patterns, and reduced electrical instability.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Choroid plexus klotho levels fall naturally with aging.
statements.evidence: these levels naturally decline with aging
statements.note: The abstract reports choroid plexus klotho levels naturally decline with aging.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Depleting klotho from the choroid plexus of young mice raised proinflammatory factor expression and drove macrophage infiltration.
statements.evidence: Depleting klotho selectively from the choroid plexus via targeted viral vector-induced knockout in Klotho flox/flox mice increased the expression of multiple proinflammatory factors and triggered macrophage infiltration of this structure in young mice
statements.note: The abstract reports klotho depletion in young mice increased proinflammatory factors and triggered macrophage infiltration.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Supplementing klotho improved cognitive performance in aged mice.
statements.evidence: Klotho depletion in aging or disease may weaken this barrier and promote immune-mediated neuropathogenesis.
statements.note: The study measures inflammatory and glial changes but never assesses cognitive or behavioral outcomes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Klotho depletion heightened hippocampal microglial activation after mice received peripheral lipopolysaccharide.
statements.evidence: Experimental depletion of klotho from the choroid plexus enhanced microglial activation in the hippocampus after peripheral injection of mice with lipopolysaccharide.
statements.note: The abstract reports klotho depletion enhanced hippocampal microglial activation following peripheral lipopolysaccharide.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: High-resolution clustering yielded 847 cell clusters, including at least 14 age-biased clusters that were mostly glial.
statements.evidence: High-resolution clustering of all cells results in 847 cell clusters and reveals at least 14 age-biased clusters that are mostly glial types.
statements.note: The abstract reports 847 clusters and at least 14 mostly glial age-biased clusters.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The hypothalamic third-ventricle ageing hub was confirmed in human brain tissue.
statements.evidence: These findings suggest that the third ventricle in the hypothalamus may be a hub for ageing in the mouse brain.
statements.note: The dataset is from mice and the abstract does not extend the hypothalamic hub finding to humans.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: With ageing, many neurons, major astrocytes, and mature oligodendrocytes decreased expression of neuronal structure and function genes.
statements.evidence: a decrease in expression of genes related to neuronal structure and function in many neuron types, major astrocyte types and mature oligodendrocytes
statements.note: The abstract reports decreased neuronal structure and function gene expression across neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Immune and some vascular cell types increased expression of genes for immune function, inflammation, and cell motility with ageing.

statements.note: The abstract reports increased immune, inflammation, and cell-motility gene expression in immune and some vascular cells.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: T-cell receptor repertoires showed the same age-related contraction as B-cell receptors.
statements.evidence: we used a phylogenetic distance metric to analyze Ig heavy-chain transcript sequences in both young and elderly individuals before and after influenza vaccination
statements.note: The study analyzes B-cell receptor (immunoglobulin) sequences only and never examines T-cell receptors.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In half of the elderly individuals, a few recall lineages filled a large repertoire space and did not decline after vaccination.
statements.evidence: In 50% of the elderly individuals, a large space in the repertoire was occupied by a small number of recall lineages that did not decline during vaccine response and contained hypermutated IgD + B cells.
statements.note: The abstract reports that in 50% of elderly individuals recall lineages occupied a large space and did not decline during the vaccine response.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with younger subjects, older subjects had a contracted naive repertoire and less intralineage diversification.
statements.evidence: older subjects demonstrated a contracted naive repertoire and diminished intralineage diversification
statements.note: The abstract reports older subjects had a contracted naive repertoire and diminished intralineage diversification relative to younger subjects.

statements.label: supported

statements.note: The abstract reports a decreased incidence of radical versus conservative mutations in elderly vaccine responses.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The PPARα agonist fenofibrate restored tissue homeostasis in aged mice.

statements.note: The abstract reports fenofibrate restored tissue homeostasis in aged mice.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Loss of type 2 cytokine signaling accelerated aging, while the IL-4–STAT6 pathway protected macrophages from senescence.
statements.evidence: type 2 cytokine signaling deficiency accelerated aging and, conversely, that the interleukin-4 (IL-4)-STAT6 pathway protected macrophages from senescence

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Activated STAT6 drove expression of DNA repair genes acting through homologous recombination and Fanconi anemia pathways.
statements.evidence: activated STAT6 promoted the expression of genes involved in DNA repair both via homologous recombination and Fanconi anemia pathways
statements.note: The abstract states activated STAT6 promoted DNA repair gene expression via homologous recombination and Fanconi anemia pathways.

statements.text: IL-4 treatment blocked macrophage senescence and improved aged mice's health span comparably to senolytics, with additive effects when combined.
